answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned tasks, with each task requiring a small bond that is forfeited if the work fails independent checks. A verifier chooses tasks after the bond is locked, so one operator cannot cheaply precompute answers for many identities. The garden may include a cedar-trimming task; its odd detail is just a signal that assignments vary. A sybil attacker must fund every identity and risk losing each bond, making mass registration costly rather than merely a matter of creating accounts.
